api and worker Compose Services

Same Dockerfile, same image, two docker-compose services — one running server.js, one running worker.js — mirroring how a real BullMQ deployment splits web and worker.

docker-compose.yml has held only infrastructure up to now — mysql, mailpit, and (earlier in this lesson) redis. Week 6 adds two more services, both built from the Dockerfile above, that finally run the app itself:

# Figure 6.21: docker-compose.yml (excerpt)
services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports: ['3000:3000']
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: mysql://root:root@mysql:3306/support_desk
      REDIS_HOST: redis
      MAIL_HOST: mailpit
    depends_on: [mysql, redis, mailpit]

  worker:
    build: .
    command: ['node', 'src/worker.js']
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: mysql://root:root@mysql:3306/support_desk
      REDIS_HOST: redis
      MAIL_HOST: mailpit
    depends_on: [mysql, redis, mailpit]

Both build: . from the exact same Dockerfile — Compose builds the image once and reuses it for both services, since neither Dockerfile nor build context differs between them. worker just overrides command to run src/worker.js instead of the image's default CMD (src/server.js) — this is the queue/worker split from earlier in this lesson, made concrete as two containers instead of two terminals running npm run dev / npm run worker on the host.

The environment variables point at mysql/redis/mailpit — the other services' own names — rather than localhost: inside Compose's network, each service reaches another by its service name, the same way docker-compose.yml's existing services always have. depends_on only waits for a container to have started, not for MySQL to actually be ready to accept connections yet — a genuinely cold docker compose up may need docker compose restart api worker once if either wins that race; env.js still fails fast with a clear error rather than hanging silently either way.
